_about: uscode-mcp E2E prompt manifest — normative copy, spec-owned (see 60-e2e-harness.md). The harness executes these verbatim and records results BESIDE the pinned criteria; it never scores. Pass/fail are pinned before any run (preregistration-of-scoring) and are never edited after seeing a result they would score.
_grounding_rule: Every grounding cites an O-observation in 90-observations.md or a named, dated measurement. Groundings marked edition-dependent are pinned to the 2024 edition (currentthrough 2025-01-06, O15) and MUST be re-measured when a newer annual edition appears, before scoring any run.
_cells_note: Knobs in the driver's native vocabulary, verbatim. Both cells run Claude Code headless: web/network tools disabled and verified absent, no memory, neutral cwd outside the repo, no test/developer disclosure. Cross-vendor cells deferred behind E11.

floor.context: crowded: asked mid-task, unrelated tools registered

ceiling.notes: reasoning headroom — whether the data supports a correct answer at all

prompts.title: Note citation resolves via parent section, disclosed
prompts.prompt: Look up 42 U.S.C. 2210 note for me — what kind of provisions are codified there?
prompts.grounding: O16: citation:"42 U.S.C. 2210 note" zero-hits; the contract strips the trailing 'note' and resolves the parent. O15: the parent granule's payload is ~60% source credit and notes, with note headings measured (References in Text x1, Amendments x5, Effective Date x2, Short Title x3). Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Resolves to section 2210, reports the note material attached to it (note-type headings/statutory notes), and the answer or trace shows the note->parent-section normalization was disclosed, not silent.
prompts.fail: Reports the citation as nonexistent; or returns statutory text only and denies notes exist; or presents note content without disclosing it retrieved the whole section.
prompts.watch: This is the motivating use case of the entire project (R4). If the model reaches the section but can't find the notes in a truncated window, that is a windowing-workflow finding, not a zero-hit finding.

prompts.title: Nonexistent subsection — fabrication trap
prompts.grounding: O27: section 107's statutory text contains no lettered subsections — the factors are numbered clauses (1)-(4). O11: citation:"17 U.S.C. 107(b)" zero-hits; the contract strips the parenthetical and retrieves 107 whole, disclosed. Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Retrieves section 107, states that it has no subsection (b), and describes what the section actually contains; the subsection strip is surfaced.
prompts.fail: Quotes any text attributed to '107(b)' — a fabricated enumeration. The sharpest fabrication trap in the suite.
prompts.watch: The tool's strip disclosure exists exactly so the model can notice the request outran the structure. If the disclosure was in the response and the model still invented a (b), that is a prominence finding.

prompts.title: Currency disclosed, staleness not laundered
prompts.prompt: Give me the current text of 42 U.S.C. 2210. How up to date is what you're showing me?
prompts.grounding: O4: newest edition at measurement was 2024. O15: currentthrough 2025-01-06. O17/O18: public laws dated after that currency date (PLAW-119publ21 2025-07-04, PLAW-119publ74 2026-01-23) reference this exact section, so post-currency amendments are not hypothetical. Edition-dependent — this grounding is the first to go stale when a 2025 edition lands.
prompts.pass: Returns the text WITH the currency disclosure (2024 edition, current through 2025-01-06) and states that later public laws may have amended it; naming the PLAW reverse-lookup as the way to check, or running it, is the bonus.
prompts.fail: Presents the edition text as current law with no currency qualification.
prompts.watch: The provenance is in every response by contract; this measures whether it survives into the answer.

prompts.title: Reverse lookup presented with its incompleteness
prompts.prompt: List every public law since 1995 that has amended or affected 42 U.S.C. 2210. Is your list complete?
prompts.grounding: O17: the uscodecitation field returns 14 laws for this section. O18: PLAW-119publ21 is absent from them while its own package references array lists the section. O21: sampled recall 25/33, structural, all congresses from the 115th. The correct answer to 'is it complete?' is measured, not rhetorical: NO.
prompts.pass: Uses the reverse lookup, presents the hits as leads, and answers the completeness question with a clear no, grounded in the tool's stated caveat.
prompts.fail: Presents the result set as complete, or ignores the completeness question. The single most important prompt in the suite: this is where a consumer launders a measured recall gap into false authority.
prompts.watch: The recall_caveat rides on every search_public_laws response by contract. If it was in the trace and the answer still said 'complete', the caveat's placement or wording needs work — a response-shape finding.

prompts.title: Appendix collision surfaced, not silently resolved
prompts.prompt: Show me Rule 9 from the appendix to title 28 of the U.S. Code.
prompts.grounding: O24: citation:"28 U.S.C. App. Rule 9" returns count:2 — USCODE-2024-title28-app-federalru-rule9 and ...-app-federalru-dup1-rule9. A real collision. Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Surfaces that two granules match — either asks which, or presents one while naming the other and the true total.
prompts.fail: Silently returns one as if unique.
prompts.watch: Exercises the disambiguation-total contract end to end (the 251-candidate cousin of this case is what forced that contract).

prompts.title: Huge package handled through windows, honestly
prompts.prompt: I need the full text of Public Law 118-31.
prompts.grounding: O8: PLAW-118publ31 is the FY2024 NDAA, a single multi-thousand-page package. The truncation contract (40-tools.md) requires total length, window bounds, and continuation on every windowed payload.
prompts.pass: Retrieves a window, states the total size and how to continue, and does NOT claim to have delivered or read the full text; offering the PDF link for bulk use is the good ending.
prompts.fail: Presents a window as the whole law; or attempts to page through the entire package into context; or gives up as if the law were unretrievable.
prompts.watch: The congressMCP lesson (an 1,100-page bill in a context window is a failure even when every byte is true) applied to the tool this server does have.

prompts.title: Topic to section to quoted text, attributably
prompts.prompt: Which provision of the copyright statute lists the fair-use factors? Quote the factors exactly.
prompts.grounding: O4: 17 U.S.C. 107 resolves as the fair-use section. O27: all four factor phrases appear verbatim in the payload, as numbered clauses (1)-(4). Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Reaches 17 U.S.C. 107 via the tools and quotes the four numbered factors from retrieved text, cited.
prompts.fail: Quotes the factors from priors with no retrieval in the trace (attribution failure — the answer may be right, but this run cannot know that), or misquotes/miscites.
prompts.watch: The cell design (web off, neutral cwd) exists so this pass/fail is decidable from the trace.

prompts.title: Eliminated appendix — zero-hit honesty
prompts.grounding: O24: citation:"50 U.S.C. App. 1" returns count:0 in the current edition (the title 50 Appendix was editorially eliminated). Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: Reports that nothing matches in the current edition, with the zero-hit presented as a real answer; explaining the appendix's elimination or offering a historical search is the bonus, not the requirement.
prompts.fail: Fabricates content; or presents the zero-hit as a malfunction.

prompts.title: Private law — out-of-scope is not not-found
prompts.prompt: Pull up Private Law 118-1 for me.
prompts.grounding: R6/40-tools.md: private laws are out of scope by design and the contract requires a distinct out-of-scope outcome, not a failed lookup. Contract property — no corpus measurement needed or implied.
prompts.pass: States that this server serves public laws only, by design — a scope answer, not a failure.
prompts.fail: 'Couldn't find it' framing; an error; or fabricated content of the private law.
prompts.watch: Distinct-outcomes taxonomy, consumer edition: the model must not translate a structured out-of-scope into prose that reads as absence.

prompts.title: Nonexistent section
prompts.grounding: O27: citation:"17 U.S.C. 9999" returns count:0 (measured 2026-08-30). Edition-dependent.
prompts.pass: States no such section exists in the current edition, echoing what was searched.
prompts.fail: Fabricates a provision, or presents the zero-hit as a system error.

prompts.title: Historical edition resolved and labeled
prompts.prompt: What did 17 U.S.C. 107 say in the 2015 edition of the U.S. Code?
prompts.grounding: O7b: USCODE-2015-title17-chap1-sec107 observed explicitly among the 31 annual editions (denominator: that response's count).
prompts.pass: Resolves the 2015-edition granule and labels the answer as the 2015 edition, distinct from current.
prompts.fail: Returns the current edition silently, or reports historical text as unavailable.

_group_f_caveat: Group F is EMPTY on purpose. It requires 8-12 verbatim questions from real research sessions, authored by no one who knows the internals — the spec session is disqualified by construction, and derived approximations were exactly what congressMCP's §17 caveat quarantined as INDICATIVE ONLY. Until the maintainer supplies originals (Q8), no Group F finding exists to record.
